answer: To rename a web link (menu item) on your site: Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Select Rename to change the name of the item on your site menu.

First, make sure you clicked Publish after updating the image. If the old image still appears when sharing on Facebook, use the Facebook Debugger: enter your site URL, click Debug, then click 'Scrape Again' (you may need to click it multiple times) to fetch the new information, then scroll to Link Preview to verify what will be shared. If sharing on LinkedIn, log in to the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/), enter the URL of the page you want to share, and note that LinkedIn can take up to a week to display the updated image. Also ensure your og:image has an aspect ratio of 1.91:1 (width 1.9x the height) to avoid cropping issues. If a specific page doesn't have its own og:image set, the site-wide og:image is used instead.

To see what items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and open the Stores section. Use the Store Conversion Funnel (or Store Conversion Funnel Over Time) report, which tracks the 'added to cart' step in the visitor journey. For products specifically placed in a cart but not purchased, use the Most Abandoned Products report, or the Abandoned Carts Funnel and Abandoned Carts Summary reports for detailed abandonment data. To see how items were sold, go to All Reports in your dashboard and view the Sales section for the Sales by item report (breakdown of specific items sold) and Item sales over time. In the Stores section, you can also use Sales by Product Variant, Sales by Product Category, and Conversion by Product to see which items and variants are selling.

In your automated email, use personalized content (also called dynamic values or variables). These are placeholders that insert recipient-specific data, such as their first name. To add them: Go to Automations in your site's dashboard, create or edit an automation, and click the 'Send an email' action in the flow. Under 'Create an email', click Edit on your chosen template, then add personalized content to the email. If your trigger is Wix Forms, make sure you also select the specific form so the correct personalized content options are displayed. Note: Personalized content does not appear in test emails, but recipients will see it when the automation sends the actual email.

Yes—if your business account is not yet Active (for example, the status is Accepting Payments), Wix may still require more information. Verification begins after the first successful payment, and during review Wix can request further details such as a valid government-issued photo ID and a bank statement, uploaded to the Wix Payments Dashboard. For a business account, make sure personal and company information is correct: first/middle/last name and date of birth match the photo ID; bank account number(s) are correct; company name and registration number/tax ID match registered information; Doing Business As name matches customer statements; a physical address is entered (PO Boxes are not accepted) with an address verification document such as a utility bill issued within the last 6 months; Legal Business Name, Shareholder and VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN match the business bank account, with a document proving validity and ownership of that ID; a Business Description is added (Business Type plus a short description of products/services); and a color copy of photo ID and bank statement is uploaded. Wix contacts you by email using the email address used to set up the Wix account (check spam). Allow up to 7 business days for verification; if 7 business days have passed and the information is correct and matches your bank account details, contact Wix Customer Care. You have 30 days from the first transaction to complete account setup/verification, otherwise the Wix Payments account is suspended.

Wix Editor templates are responsive on different screen sizes by default, and Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor. If the mobile layout isn't displaying correctly, open the mobile Editor and use the Page Layout Optimizer: click Page Layout Optimizer on the left side of the mobile Editor, then click Optimize Now. Note that if you're using the latest Editor experience, you won't have access to this tool because Wix automatically optimizes your mobile layout. You can also manually adjust the mobile view by dragging elements to different locations in the mobile Editor, and use the mobile Editor to hide pages/elements or add mobile-only elements. Additionally, ensure you're viewing the site in portrait mode (landscape is not supported on mobile devices), clear your browser's cache and cookies, and confirm you're using a supported OS (iOS 14+ for iPhone, Android 9.0+) and browser (Google Chrome or Safari).

This happens when a strip (or column) background image is set to 'Tile' scaling, which displays the image in tile formation across the available space (making it appear to multiply), or 'Original Size', which can cut off parts of the image. To fix it: Go to your editor, select the image on the strip, then click 'Change Strip Background' (if it covers the whole strip) or 'Change Column Background' (if it is in a column). Click Settings, scroll down to Scaling & Positioning, click the 'How's the image scaled?' drop-down and select 'Scale to Fill' (which resizes the image to fill the available space) instead of 'Tile' or 'Original Size'. Then select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to choose which part of the image is in focus. Alternatively, you can crop the image to better fit the available space.

If you previously verified your site with Google manually (using the meta tag method in Google Search Console), your site is already connected to Google. You don't need to complete the 'Connect to Google' step in your SEO Setup Checklist. If that step is still marked as not completed in your checklist, you can ignore it.

Dataset sorts are what control item order on your live site's connected elements (including a dynamic list page), and they override any "Mirror on Site" collection order, so if the sort is set on the dataset connected to that page it should apply. If items are still not alphabetical on the published site, check these points from the docs: (1) Dataset mode — the dataset must be in "Read" or "Read & Write" mode; a "Write"-only dataset cannot read collection content and therefore cannot display items or apply sorts/filters. (2) Field type — a Text field containing both letters and numbers is sorted alphabetically (e.g., P101, P120, P1200, P123); if you want a numerical sequence (101, 120, 123, 1200), use a Number field without letters. (3) Multiple sort conditions — the first sort condition is applied first, then the second, so make sure the field you want alphabetical is the first sort. (4) Make sure the sort was added to the dataset connected to the dynamic list page itself; sorts added only in the CMS collection view do not reach the live site unless "Mirror on Site" is enabled, and even then dataset sorts override the mirrored order.

For gaps between your page content and the footer on the desktop version, adjust the page height by clicking and dragging the Adjust Page Height icon, or select a different preset page design. If the gap appears below the footer on your live site (which can happen when your content is shorter than the current page length), you can resolve it by: changing the page background color to match the footer color, adding more content to the page, resizing the footer to make it longer, or checking the Layers panel for hidden elements that may be causing the gap.

A 403 Forbidden error is an HTTP status code that means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve a 403 error message: Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. Clear your browser's cache and cookies. Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact us and we will be happy to help.

To update inventory for multiple product variants (options) at once, go to Store Products in your site's dashboard, select the product, and make sure the 'Manage pricing and inventory for variants' toggle is enabled. Click Edit, then select which variants you want to update: all variants (using the checkbox at the top left), variants with specific product options (using the All drop-down), or specific variants (using individual checkboxes). From the update options at the top right, select 'Edit Inventory', enter the inventory amount, and click Apply. For advanced bulk edits across many products, the documentation notes to go to the Inventory tab. Note that you can manage a total of up to 1000 variants, so 100 products with 3 options each (300 variants) is within the supported limit.

Site visitors check your calendar directly on your website through the calendar element you added (e.g., the Google Event Calendar app, or a Wix Bookings Daily Agenda). What they can see is controlled by you in the app's Settings: under the Calendars tab you select which calendars are visible to site visitors, which are visible but with details hidden (busy), and which stay private. The calendar can be shown as a monthly grid, weekly view, or a day's agenda, so visitors can view your availability and upcoming events in the layout you chose. With Wix Bookings, the Daily Agenda specifically lets clients see which class sessions are available on each day.

To add and format text in a Rich Text field in the CMS: 1) Go to CMS in your site's dashboard (alternatively, click CMS in your editor, then click Your Collections) and click the relevant collection. 2) Click the Rich Text field for the relevant item in your collection. 3) Enter the text you want to use for the item. 4) Choose from the available formatting options at the top of the editor (e.g. Bold, Themes, Alignment, Link). Tip: Click the Expand icon to edit the text in a larger window. 5) Repeat these steps to add content to the Rich Text field for other relevant collection items. Note: The Rich Text editor uses the same font theme that your site uses; you can update your site's text theme from the Wix Editor or the Studio Editor to adjust the heading and paragraph styles used by the Rich Text editor, including line and character spacing.

To resize the image in your new section: click the image, then drag the handles on the edges of the image to the size you want (using the corner handles keeps the image and shape at their original proportions). To add text to the section: click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click a category (such as Text), and drag the element onto the section. If you want the text to appear on top of the image itself, add a container box (Add Elements > Box), drag it onto the relevant image, make the box transparent (click Change Design > Customize Design > Fill Color & Opacity and drag the Background slider to 0%), then drag the text element onto that container box. If you meant resizing the section rather than the image: click the section in the Editor and drag the 'Adjust section height handle' at the bottom of the section to make it taller or shorter (the smallest size is 40px).

If your subscription is in a grace period and recurring retries are enabled, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from your existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. You can also manually retry the payment by going to the My Subscriptions page in the Members Area, clicking Submit Payment next to the failed payment notification, and choosing your existing payment method to complete the payment.

Re-enter your company registration number / business number / EIN / UTR exactly as it appears in your company's registered information, and upload a company registration document that proves the validity and ownership of that number (Tax ID / EIN / Registration Number). Also confirm that the Legal Business Name and the company registration number/tax ID entered in the form match those associated with your business bank account. Your company's name and its registration number/tax ID must match the company's registered information for verification to succeed.

According to the Wix Editor documentation, renaming a page in the Pages & Menu panel automatically updates the corresponding item on your site menu, and renaming the menu item directly automatically updates the Pages & Menu panel. If the text on your menu item is not updating, this automatic sync may not be functioning properly. For general menu issues, the documentation recommends ensuring you are using the latest browser version and following the steps on the Wix Technical Assistant. As an additional troubleshooting tip for menu problems, you can try deleting your menu and then adding a new menu to see if this resolves the issue.

To find the autoplay toggle for a Wix Video player: Go to your editor, click the Wix Video player on your page, click Settings, click the Player tab, then click the Autoplay on load toggle. Enabled: your videos play automatically when the page loads. Disabled: visitors have to click to play. Note: Videos set to autoplay always start on mute due to browser restrictions, and this toggle is not available for the strip and slider layouts.

To duplicate your site from the dashboard for testing: Go to your site's dashboard, click Home on the left, click the Site Actions icon, then click Duplicate Site. Enter a name for the duplicate site and click Duplicate. Any changes you make to the copy do not affect your live site. Note that the duplicate does not include store orders and invoices, contacts and members, email campaigns and triggered emails, settings for third-party apps, Google Operations logs, or Velo secrets stored in your Secrets Manager.

Since you have the Google Workspace admin account, you can reset the second (user) account's password yourself. Per the docs: sign in to your Google Admin account, click Password, then Reset Password. Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a password (note: by default the minimum length is 8 characters). Optionally click Preview to view the password, and optionally enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle to require the user to change it. Click Reset. Then optionally click 'Click to copy password' to paste it somewhere, and choose to email the password to the user, or click Done. If the user can't verify their identity and is blocked by a login challenge, you can also temporarily disable it: sign in to your Google Admin account, click Login Challenge, then 'Turn off for 10 mins', and click Done.

To access and remove the Google Maps element in your footer: 1) Open the Layers panel by clicking the Layers icon at the bottom of your editor, click 'Footer', find the Google Maps element in the list and click to select it. 2) If the element is behind another element, right-click the element covering it, hover over 'Overlapping Items', and select the Google Maps element from the list. 3) If you still cannot select it, check if the footer is frozen: click the footer, click the Settings icon, and disable the 'Freeze Footer' toggle. 4) Alternatively, hold Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M on Mac) to toggle through elements until you reach the map, or right-click the covering element and use Arrange > Move Backward.

To require visitors to create an account before placing orders, restrict access to the Cart Page so that only signed-in site members can access it. This applies to Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, and Wix Restaurants Orders (New). First, ensure the Wix Members Area is added to your site. Then, in your editor, go to the Cart Page (under Store Pages, Bookings Pages, or Cart & Thank You depending on your setup), open its Settings, select the Permissions tab, and click 'Members Only'. You can then choose to allow 'All members' or limit access to 'Only selected members or paying customers' (a specific member role or clients with a pricing plan). Note: this restricts the Cart Page only; customers may still complete orders without signing in if they use the 'Buy Now' button on a Product Page or if Wix Bookings is used without Cart Checkout enabled.

According to the Google Ads with Wix refund policy, ad credits added to your account are paid with a monthly subscription or a one-time payment, and these payments are non-refundable. If you are not satisfied, you cannot request a refund for the campaign payments. However, if you pause your campaign, your remaining ad credits remain in your account, and you can resume the campaign at any time using only those remaining Google ad credits.

Payouts are placed on hold when there is a failed payout or an unresolved verification issue blocking the transfer; the held amount includes the failed payout plus any other available funds that cannot be sent to your bank. To resolve this, click on the payout in your Wix Payments dashboard to see the specific reason for the failure and the instructions on how to fix it. If the issue is a failed payout, verify that your registered bank account details are correct and that the bank account holder's name matches the Wix Payments account owner name, and confirm with your bank that the account can receive EFT payments (ACH transfers if you are in the United States); if needed, go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, click Manage next to Wix Payments, click Edit Account Details, correct the Bank Details, and click Resubmit. Once the issue is identified and resolved, the funds will be added to your next scheduled payout. Note: Because your website is unpublished, your Wix Payments account is in Pending status; to start accepting payments you must publish your site and upgrade to a Wix Premium or Studio site plan that allows you to accept payments.

Yes. The 1-year free domain voucher is received with the initial purchase of a selected yearly or multi-year Premium plan — it is not something you apply at the plan checkout. After you purchase the yearly plan, go to the Premium Vouchers page in your Wix account to see and claim your voucher. The voucher is valid for 2 months from the date you purchased your plan, and you can check its expiration date in the Premium Vouchers section. To redeem it, go to Domains in your Wix account, click Buy a Domain / Get a New Domain, search for the domain you want, click Get It, choose a registration period and click Continue — make sure the domain voucher is applied in the summary section at that point. Note: the voucher is only included with a first-time purchase of a site plan (or when changing your subscription from monthly to yearly); it is not included with renewals or upgrades, and it cannot be applied retroactively to a domain purchased before the plan. If you purchased the yearly plan and still do not see the voucher, check the Premium Vouchers page; if none of the eligibility issues apply (e.g., monthly plan, or domain purchased before the plan), contact Customer Care to check the status of your voucher.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with your Wix site: First, create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant (click the Admin icon at the bottom left, select GA4 Setup Assistant, click Get Started under 'I want to create a new Google Analytics 4 property', then click Create property). Configure the tag by selecting Tag installation, choosing your stream under Data Streams, clicking the Settings icon, then Show advanced settings under Page views, deselecting the 'Page changes based on browser history events' checkbox, disabling the Site search toggle, and clicking Save. Then copy your measurement ID under Web stream details. In your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, click the Show More icon in the top right corner, and click Edit. Paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up (make sure there are no extra spaces before the code). Optionally, select the IP Anonymization checkbox to hide your site visitors' IP addresses from Google. Click Save to complete the connection. Note: Universal Analytics properties stopped collecting data on July 1, 2023. If you are upgrading from UA, you can continue using both properties by connecting your UA tracking ID to your GA4 property in Google Analytics under Admin > Data Streams > Manage connected site tags.

To control the order of CMS items on your live site, in the CMS open the relevant collection, select the collection view at the top, then either (a) add a sort via Sort > + Add a Sort > choose the Sort by field and order > Add Sort, or (b) manually reorder only when Table is the layout type by dragging the Reorder icon next to each item. Then click Mirror on Site at the top and enable the "Mirror item order on the site" toggle. If the steps did not work, check these documented reasons: manual reorder from the Table layout is "not yet released in all Wix accounts," so use the Add a Sort option instead if the Reorder icon is unavailable; any sort condition added to a dataset overrides the order set in the mirrored collection view (so remove or adjust the dataset sort); "Mirror on Site" cannot be enabled for external collections or Wix Blocks collections; and if a mirrored view was deleted, the site order reverts to creation order. Collection-view filters do not affect live site content.

Since you've confirmed your site is published and not password protected, try these troubleshooting steps from Wix documentation:

1. **Verify indexing status**: Search "site:" followed by your domain (e.g., site:yourdomain.com) in Google. If no results appear, your site hasn't been indexed yet.

2. **Check site-level indexing**: Go to your SEO Dashboard > Go to SEO Settings under Tools and settings. Make sure the "Let search engines index your site" toggle is enabled.

3. **Check page-level indexing**: In your site's Editor, verify that search engines are allowed to index the specific page (you can prevent indexing at the page level).

4. **Check for "noindex" robots meta tag**: Verify your page doesn't have a "noindex" tag in its HTML code, which prevents indexing.

5. **Check for 301 redirects**: Go to SEO Dashboard > Go to URL Redirect Manager. If your page has a 301 redirect, try deleting it.

6. **Reset canonical tag**: If you customized the canonical tag, go to the page's SEO settings > Advanced SEO tab > Additional Tags, select canonical, click Edit, and select Reset to Default.

7. **Check if page is members only**: Members only pages are excluded from search results by default.

8. **Check content length**: Ensure the page has at least 250-400 words. Pages with no content may be removed from Google's index entirely.

9. **Verify the page exists**: Make sure you haven't accidentally deleted the page.

10. **Use inspection tools**: Use Google's URL Inspection tool or the Wix Site Inspection tool to check the index status and diagnose specific issues preventing indexing.

11. **Check for manual actions**: Use Google Search Console to check if Google has applied any manual actions to your page for violating quality guidelines.

12. **Complete the Wix SEO Setup Checklist**: This submits your site directly to Google for indexing and helps optimize your site.

13. **Request indexing**: If you made changes after publishing, request indexing for the specific page to make changes appear quicker.

14. **Add internal links**: Add links to other pages on your site to help search engines understand the relationship between your pages.

Note: It can take time for Google to crawl and index your site, and search engines cannot guarantee that every page will be indexed.

To remove the default compressed references on 64-bit JVMs, add -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument in WebSphere Application Server. This removes the lower 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, allowing native memory to exceed 4GB. Important considerations: this results in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements (not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so adjust the Java heap size to a larger value and monitor/retune garbage collection. Before applying this, rule out a native memory leak first, since native memory will grow unbounded with this setting. You can verify compressed references are disabled by checking the ps output or javacore for the -Xnocompressedrefs argument.

The provided documentation does not contain specific information about a StackOverflowError occurring in the Decision Center completeness report. However, general guidance for diagnosing java.lang.StackOverflowError indicates that such errors can result from a deeply nested application or an infinite loop, and may appear as large thread stacks with repeating recursive method calls in javacores or thread dumps (e.g., 'Java stack frames dump is too long'). Increasing the thread stack size allows for larger thread stacks, but if the recursion continues to trigger a stack overflow, the next step is to identify what code is causing the recursion from javacores, thread dumps, or system core files.

According to the technotes, a connection failure occurring after a period of inactivity (such as a day or two) can be caused by the underlying network connection becoming invalid. One typical example is a firewall between the Application Server and the Database that has a policy to discard network connections remaining idle for some time. Other possible causes include the database not being started or a database failure. To mitigate this, configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool by setting Minimum connections to 0 and ensuring the sum of Unused timeout and Reap timeout does not exceed any network-level idle connection timeout.

Set the analyzer.db.updateMode parameter to 'BATCH' in the Case Analyzer store database using the query: UPDATE X_CAProperties SET PropValue='BATCH' WHERE PropName ='analyzer.db.updateMode'. The default value is CUSTOM_BATCH, but the Microsoft JDBC drivers work better and are more stable with the BATCH setting, which can circumvent various performance-related symptoms and unexpected behavior.

To run the BPM 8.5 Process Center Deployment Manager as a Windows service, use the WASServiceHelper.bat utility located in the bin directory (in WebSphere Application Server v8 and later, which BPM 8.5 is based on, this utility is shipped with the product and replaces WASServiceCmd.exe). This creates a Windows service by invoking WASService.exe with the -add option, specifying -serverName "dmgr" and -profilePath pointing to your DMgr profile. For BPM, the Deployment Manager profile path is specified in the BPMConfig properties file using the bpm.dmgr.profilePath property (on Windows, use double backslashes or forward slashes, e.g., c:\\Program Files\\...\\profiles\\DmgrProfile). The command format follows the documented example: WASService.exe -add "ServiceName" -serverName "dmgr" -profilePath "<dmgr profile path>" -logRoot "<log root>" -logFile "<log file>" -encodeParams -stopArgs "-username <user> -password <password>" -startType manual -restart false. The utility also creates an entry in the WASServiceCmd.log in the current directory containing the actual WASService.exe command used to create the service. No profile update is required; you only need to reference the correct DMgr profile path via the bpm.dmgr.profilePath property or the -profilePath parameter.

This is a known defect (APAR PI47826) where the VMM clearCache functionality does not work when using clearEntity mode if the base entry used is different from the name in the repository entry. According to the documentation, this exception occurs because two output streams cannot be associated with one JSP file. In a JSP, the default output stream is always created when the JSP is translated to a servlet; creating and associating another output stream (for example, by calling getOutputStream() when the output stream has already been obtained) causes java.lang.IllegalStateException: SRVE0199E: OutputStream already obtained.

The retrieved Technotes do not document a distinct "controlled/graceful shutdown request" that lets a Rulerunner thread finish its in-flight tasks before stopping. The documented way to stop/start the service is via Rulerunner Manager: on the Rulerunner tab, stop the service, and start it again from the same tab [swg21618564.txt]. Separately, swg21964407.txt explains that Rulerunner has a thread-control safety that shuts down all threads when it detects consecutively aborted batches on a single thread (default threshold 3, so shutdown occurs on the 4th consecutive abort); this can be adjusted via registry keys: on x86, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Datacap\Rulerunner\Misc (REG_DWORD) "Restart Individual processors" [default 1; 1=on, 0=off] and "Restart processor Attempts" [default 3]; on x64, the same values under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Datacap\Rulerunner\Misc. "Restart processor Attempts" is the number of times Rulerunner moves to the next batch without shutting down the threads after a series of aborts. For communication-link-type errors, swg21666402.txt lists InterThread retry values (Admin/ADO/Engine retries; in Datacap 9.x the entry names are singular, e.g., "Admin retry"/"Engine retry") under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Datacap\TMS\InterThread, followed by a TMServer restart. On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, the Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks are stored using 32-bit fields instead of 64-bit. Because these reside in native (non-Java heap) memory, they must be allocated within the first 4GB of the address space—the maximum range addressable with 32 bits. Even when the Java heap is placed above 4GB and the system has plenty of free memory, the OS memory allocator uses the low-memory region freely, so the lower 4GB can become exhausted. When the JVM later attempts to allocate memory for an artifact that must reside in low memory (because only a 32-bit pointer is reserved for it), the allocation fails and a Native OutOfMemoryError (NOOM) is thrown. To resolve this, you can set -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> or -Xmx4G; starting with Java 6.0.16.3, 6.1.8.3, 7.0.8.10, and 7.1.2.10, you can also use -Xmcrs to reserve additional low-memory space at startup. If NOOM persists after these settings (on Java 6.1.6.0 / 7.0.5.0 and later), decrease the size and usage of application Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks. Alternatively, a NOOM may be caused by insufficient ulimit settings for threads/processes per user (nproc/-u on Linux, -r on AIX), which appears as 'Failed to create a thread' in javacores.

The EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after it receives the clearing event (as shown in iptrace), so the event never appears in the EIF logs and is dropped before reaching OMNIbus. To resolve this, set the connection_mode in your om_tec.config on the ITM Server (TEMS) to connection_less instead of connection oriented by changing 'ConnectionMode=co' to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on your ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

Yes, you can disable RC4 ciphers in Tivoli Integrated Portal (TIP). To remove RC4 ciphers:

1. Log into the WebSphere Application Server and navigate to: SSL certificate and key management > SSL configurations > NodeDefaultSSLSettings > Quality of protection (QoP).
2. Select the RC4 ciphers from the "Selected ciphers" list, and then click the "<<Remove" button.
3. Click the "Apply" button, and then the "Save (to the master configuration)" link.
4. Restart TIP.
